title: Expeditionary Airfield and Emergency Services Officer (III) (CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
1. MOS 7002, Expeditionary Airfield and Emergency Services Officer (III)
(CWO5 to WO) PMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. The Expeditionary Airfield and Emergency Services Officer
conducts planning for and oversees the installation, operation, and
maintenance of airfield surfacing materials, expeditionary visual landing
aids, and aircraft recovery equipment. In addition, these officers conduct
the planning for and direct structural and aircraft firefighting, rescue, and
salvage and recovery operations.

       b.    Prerequisites

        (1) This MOS may only be assigned to warrant officers who previously
were qualified in one of the following enlisted MOSs 7011 and 7051.

        (2) Must meet the medical standards as required per reference (bc),
The National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 1582 and reference (cq), The
Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) 29 Code of Federal
Regulation (CFR) 1910.234.

       c.    Requirements

        (1) Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course (WOBC) (M02RMN4) within
18 months of appointment to WO.

             (2) WO:

            (a) Complete the Marine Expeditionary Airfield Advance Course
(N2370L2) at NAS, Pensacola, FL.

            (b) Complete the Marine Expeditionary Airfield Equipment Course
(N2370D2) at NAS, Pensacola, FL.

            (c) Complete the Fire Protection Apprentice (Air Force) Course
(F0764T2) at Goodfellow Air Force Base, San Angelo, TX.

            (d) Complete the Marine Survey and Assault Zone Assessment
(MSAAZA) Course at MAWTS-1 Yuma, AZ.

             (3) CWO2 to CWO5:

            (a) Complete the MAWTS-1, Weapons and Tactics Instructors Course
(M149731) at MAWTS-1 Yuma, AZ.

            (b) Complete the Contingency Airfield Pavement Evaluation (CAPE)
Course, Air Force Civil Engineer Support Agency Tyndall, Air Force Base, FL.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (dp), Marine Expeditionary Airfield/Emergency Services Officers
(EAESO) Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Airfield Operations Specialists 53-2022.

       f.    Related Military Skill.   None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
